statement: A rigid transformation (also called Euclidean transformation or Euclidean isometry) is a geometric transformation g of a Euclidean space that preserves the Euclidean distance between every pair of points, d(g(X), g(Y))^2 = d(X, Y)^2, formally producing for any vector v a transformed vector of the form T(v) = R v + t, where R is an orthogonal transformation matrix satisfying R^T = R^{-1} and t is a translation vector.

symbols.meaning: vector in the Euclidean vector space
transformed vector under the rigid transformation
orthogonal transformation matrix satisfying R^T = R^{-1}
vector giving the translation of the origin
Euclidean distance between points X and Y

properties.property: Distance preservation: d(g(X), g(Y))^2 = d(X, Y)^2 for all points X and Y
properties.why: a rigid transformation by definition preserves the Euclidean distance between every pair of points

properties.property: Orthogonality condition for linear part: [L]^T [L] = [I], implying det([L]) = ±1
properties.why: preserving the distance squared requires (v - w)^T [L]^T [L] (v - w) = (v - w)^T (v - w)

properties.property: Proper rigid transformations (rigid motions) satisfy det(R) = +1
properties.why: preserves handedness and orientation by excluding reflections
the transformation includes a reflection, transforming a left hand into a right hand

properties.property: Group structure: rigid transformations form E(n), and proper rigid transformations form SE(n)
properties.why: rigid transformations form the Euclidean group and rigid motions form the special Euclidean group under composition
any rigid transformation is a composition of an orthogonal transformation and a translation

properties.property: Every rigid motion in dimension three can be decomposed as a rototranslation and is a screw motion
properties.why: consequence of Chasles' theorem in dimension three

properties.property: Shape and size preservation under proper rigid transformation
properties.why: any object retains the same shape and size under distance- and handedness-preserving motions

assumptions.assumption: Euclidean space R^n equipped with standard Euclidean distance metric
assumptions.breaks_when: space is non-Euclidean or distance metric is not the scalar product distance

assumptions.assumption: Linear part R is orthogonal (R^T R = I)
assumptions.breaks_when: transformation introduces non-uniform scaling, stretching, or shear deformations

assumptions.assumption: det(R) = +1 when defining a proper rigid transformation / rigid motion
assumptions.breaks_when: transformation contains a reflection (det(R) = -1), which reverses handedness

failure_modes.cause: Transformation matrix is not orthogonal, introducing scaling or shear
Orthogonal matrix produces a reflection, inverting the orientation of objects
